# A Training-Time Diagnostic for Generalization via the Log-Alignment Ratio

**Shehper & Vaswani — "A Training-Time Diagnostic for Generalization via the Log-Alignment Ratio"** · arXiv:2605.28975 (v1) · serialisation: the native arXiv HTML, converted with page marks against the arXiv PDF (task-008, 2026-08).

**An external work; the abstract is given.** The subject of the paper is the LAR diagnostic (a measure of parameter-activation alignment) from parameterization theory; the authors expressly decline any claim to a new theory of grokking. Grokking is a test bench; what the corpus values here is the link between the LAR and the fall of the effective dimension of the learned function. Set aside by the triage of task-021 (2026-08-26). No work of the corpus cites it yet. The introduction and the quoted paragraphs are translated lazily, as quotations appear (decision D2-b). The original — [`original/`](original/2605.28975.a-training-time-diagnostic-for-generalization-via-the-log-alignment-ratio.md); the analysis of the claims is the neighbouring `…claims.txt`.

# Abstract

*"We study the log-alignment ratio (LAR), a measure of parameter–activation alignment, introduced in parameterization theory. We reformulate it as the overlap between a weight spectrum $p$ of the normalized squared singular values of a matrix and an activation spectrum $q$ of the normalized squared projections of inputs onto its singular directions. We show that unembedding LAR tracks the transition between memorization and generalization in two different settings by capturing the spread of $p$ and $q$ during training. In grokking, LAR predicts the effective dimension of the learned function: $k\approx n^{2(1-\mathrm{LAR})}$, where $n$ is the input dimension of the matrix. In 3B-parameter language model pre-training, its deviation from a non-overfitting baseline tracks the generalization gap, and its rate of decline increases as overfitting approaches. LAR is computable from quantities available in the forward pass with negligible overhead and requires no held-out validation data."*
